extracted.intended_audience: short-story writers, magazine editors, literary critics, and readers interested in anthology selection/standards
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial selection and evaluation criteria for choosing short stories for an annual 'best of' anthology, based on an impartial reading of stories published in American periodicals and judged by tests of substance and form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of Substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The first qualitative test: report upon how vitally compelling the writer makes his selected facts or incidents. Substance is something achieved by the artist in every act of creation; facts in a story only obtain substantial embodiment when the artist's power of compelling imaginative persuasion transforms them into a living truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the story attains imaginative life — does the writer transform selected facts into a 'living truth' that compels the reader? This is the most vital test; if a story survives it, it has imaginative life. Examples/notes: substance is not mere factual reporting but the imaginative persuasion that renders facts substantial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of Form
rubrics_metrics.description: The second qualitative test: whether the writer shapes the living substance into the most beautiful and satisfying form by skilful selection and arrangement of material and by direct and appealing presentation in portrayal and characterization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess skillful arrangement, selection, and the directness/appeal of presentation (portrayal and characterization). A story that survives the form test demonstrates technique that enhances substance — producing a satisfying artistic whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-standard evaluation (substance + form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories are judged by the double standard of substance and form: each story is examined impartially, surrendering to the writer's point of view and, granting his choice of material and interpretation, tested by both standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological instructions: read stories 'in a critical spirit' but attempt to surrender to the writer's POV; grant the author's chosen material and interpretation; then apply the two tests. The editor reports having read over 2,200 short stories and examined each impartially according to this double standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification & asterisk scoring system
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories fall into four groups indicated in the year-book index by asterisk notation: no asterisk (fail either test), one asterisk (survive either substance or form), two asterisks (survive both tests and merit a second reading), three asterisks (highest distinction; Roll of Honor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation of marks: no asterisk = story fails to survive either test and is listed without comment; * = survives one test (either substance or form); ** = survives both tests and may claim a second reading; *** = finest distinction, listed in a special 'Roll of Honor'. The two-asterisk category is explicitly tied to 'claim to a second reading.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for Roll of Honor (three asterisks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that unite genuine substance and artistic form in a closely woven pattern with spiritual sincerity so earnest, and a creative belief so strong, that each may fairly claim a position of some permanence in literature as a criticism of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the highest evaluative standard: look for unity of substance and form, close patterning, spiritual sincerity, and strong creative belief; such stories are judged likely to have permanence and literary significance. The editor notes that some titles in this list also carry a further asterisk indicating personal preference for ultimate preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-reading as a quality indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: A story of greater distinction should lay convincing claim to a second reading — taken as evidence that it has survived both tests and has depth/complexity warranting re-reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use re-readability as a practical test for higher distinction (explicitly tied to the two-asterisk group). If a story rewards a second reading, it has characteristics (depth, craft, layered meaning) that mark it above ordinary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection rules / procedural constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical editorial rules applied to selection: do not republish an English story or a story whose immediate book-form publication seems likely; include no more than one story by an individual author in the volume; focus on stories published in American periodicals within the covered years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope and fairness constraints: the editor states it 'has been a point of honor' not to republish English stories or ones likely to appear in book form, and a rule limiting one story per author. The selection is confined to stories published in American magazines in 1914–1915 and is based on reading a very large sample (~2,200 stories). These rules affect which stories are eligible independent of pure literary merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial critical method / reviewer stance
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor's method: examine each story impartially, surrender to the writer's point of view, grant his choice of material and interpretation, and test by the standards of substance and form while permitting no conscious personal preference or prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluator conduct guidance: attempt to adopt the author's vantage to judge effectiveness; avoid conscious bias, although the editor admits occasional personal preferences (marked separately). This prescribes how critics/selectors should approach reading and judging submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of commercial bias and preference for artistic integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: A stated qualitative preference for artistic craft over commercialized fiction: prefer writers who shape materials passionately to a creative purpose and editors who will welcome artistic craftsmen rather than commercialized short-story tradesmen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not a mechanical scoring rule, this criterion signals an evaluative tendency to favor literary sincerity, originality, and artistic labor over formulaic/commercial writing (e.g., scenario-driven or 'movie' oriented work). It informs judgment about what counts as 'genuine substance' and 'artistic form.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication of personal preference marking
rubrics_metrics.description: Some titles in the final Roll of Honor carry an additional asterisk that reveals a personal preference of the editor for ultimate preservation, separate from the objective three-asterisk evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency note: the editor openly marks certain stories with an extra asterisk to indicate subjective preference for preservation, acknowledging that while he 'permitted no personal preference' consciously, some choices reflect his tastes.
